s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic illness with mental status changes, abdominal symptoms, respiratory distress, and cardiovascular instability
salient_findings: Hypoxia with SpO₂ of 88% on room air
key_facts: 64-year-old man
Medical history of dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, peripheral artery disease, and coronary artery disease
Previous percutaneous coronary intervention to the left anterior descending and right coronary artery
Leukocyte count of 13.4 × 10⁹/L
Sodium level of 129 mmol/L
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin of 102 μg/L
Elevated N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide of 1098 ng/L
Positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine
Negative SARS-CoV-2 and influenza tests
Chest radiograph showing right-sided lung infiltrates

ECG findings of sinus tachycardia, old incomplete right bundle branch block, new left posterior fascicular block, multifocal PVCs, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, and fascicular ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Severe Legionnaires' disease
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, and evidence of cardiac dysfunction

shortlist.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hypoxia, fever, and right-sided lung infiltrates on chest radiograph

raw.rationale: The patient has a positive Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 antigen in urine, which is a specific indicator of Legionnaires' disease, along with symptoms of pneumonia (fever, hypoxia, and right-sided lung infiltrates on chest radiograph) and systemic involvement (abdominal pain, diarrhea, and mental status changes)

rejected.label: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated troponin and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, the primary cause of these findings is more likely related to the direct effects of Legionnaires' disease rather than a separate cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has hypoxia and lung infiltrates, the diagnosis of ARDS is not specific enough to explain the full range of symptoms and laboratory findings

rejected.label: Septic shock
rejected.why: The patient does not have hypotension, which is a key component of septic shock, and the focus of the diagnosis should be on the specific infectious agent (Legionella) rather than a general septic shock diagnosis

rejected.label: Myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
rejected.why: The coronary angiography shows stable findings, and the echocardiography and cardiac MRI do not indicate a new myocardial infarction as the primary cause of the patient's condition
